mil5.1.1:0.4: 1. Question on the Fruitfulness of Offerings Made
mil5.1.1:1.1: Then King Milinda, having been given leave, bowed down at the venerable one's feet and placing his joined palms in salutation, said this:
mil5.1.1:1.3: ‘If the Buddha accepts homage, then the Buddha has not attained final Nibbāna, is fettered to the world, existing in the world, sharing in the world—therefore an offering made to him is not in vain but fruitful.
mil5.1.1:1.4: If he has attained final Nibbāna, is disconnected from the world, departed from all existences, then worship does not reach him; one who has attained final Nibbāna accepts nothing, and an offering made to one who accepts nothing is in vain and fruitless.’ This is a two-horned dilemma; it is not within the scope of those of limited understanding—this is within the scope only of the great ones. Break through this net of views and establish it on one side. This question has come to you; give sight to the future sons of the Conqueror for the refutation of opposing doctrines.”
